question: Should the final-request guards and post-execution state-credential renewal ship together on the current head after exact-head checks, or should maintainers split or soak the rollout?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the failure boundary for authoritative GitHub writes and durable repair publication; tests support the combined design, but rollout scope and tolerance for fail-closed operational interruptions remain maintainer choices.

options.title: Land the combined safety boundary
options.body: Finish the draft and exact-head checks, then merge the guarded writes and credential renewal together so every deferred mutation and publication uses the same fail-closed contract.

options.title: Split credential renewal
options.body: Separate the workflow credential-rebinding portion for independent rollout if maintainers want to isolate durable-publication availability risk from mutation authorization safety.

options.title: Keep the draft for soak
options.body: Leave the PR open while exercising the current head against representative repair clusters and reviewing rejected or unknown receipt behavior.

recommendation.title: Land the combined safety boundary
recommendation.body: Finish the draft and exact-head checks, then merge the guarded writes and credential renewal together so every deferred mutation and publication uses the same fail-closed contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns both the merged review-activity foundation and the current repair mutation-boundary implementation, making them the strongest available rollout-routing candidate.
